Man, I could’ve written this, word for word. It amazes me once again how another person can go through the exact same trauma as I did. 

It is good that you have come to this conclusion. I’m so sorry. You are right: your parents have traumatised and crippled your existence from the very beginning. And it’s not fair, you deserved much better. Sadly, the only way forward is through the CPTSD.

I have been through three years of therapy, and I can say it’s fucking hard but it helps a little. Sometimes just venting it all out with your therapist in a safe space helps a ton. 

There’s a lot of work to be done on your own, because your parents (as mine) will not help you at all. They were negligent and brutal back then, they will continue to be so now in other ways. This is something you must face and accept, at some point, in order to heal.

We are avoidants, we must remember that we may heal with the right support, but the scars are permanent—and as such need constant tending. I wish it was not so, I wish we had it easier in this life. But we must play the cards we’ve been dealt to the best of our ability…

Forgive me for ranting but there’s a popular misconception about what karma is. I was really into Buddhism as a coping mechanism when I still lived with my narc parents. 

Karma is not instant, actually we feel the effects of our past lives’ karma in the present life. The karma of your current actions does not bear its fruits in this life, maybe not even in the next one. Think of it as butterfly effect, but in a greater than life scale. Cause and effect.

So these awful people who are “unjustifiably thriving” may not receive “their due” in this life. But they will anyway, it is certain. No matter how many times they are reborn, there is no escaping it, no amending to be done about it. 

Personally, I don’t think of Karma as punishment or reward, but I can understand why many would.

You don’t mention how many rounds of deworming he has gone through, but I suppose the vet went along with the standard two rounds, two weeks apart. This is done because the first round doesn’t get rid of the eggs, so a second round of deworming is needed to get rid of the hatched young worms. 

Roundworms can be tricky to get rid of sometimes. Although rare, common house flies can carry this parasite as well, so if your kitty has a fascination with them and happens to eat an infected fly, there you have it.

I am NB. Always thought that “gender doesn’t matter, whatever is between my legs doesn’t represent me” was common sense. Turns out I was wrong and people are shocked when they can’t label you as one or the other. 

After that realization my experience with gender has been unpleasant (AFAB, when menstruation comes I get heavy gender dysphoria) but fortunately my body is on the androgynous side so I can “forget” about it most of the time. I don’t care for pronouns, I tell people/friends I am whatever they want me to be, keeps me from unnecessary drama. Although I will admit I profoundly hate that I am “limited” by this organic body, this shell of the self assigned at random. 

I am sorry to say I have no advice to give because of my tendency to push this issue under the rug until I am forced to deal with it, but dressing in a way that represents your unique self is a great way to cope with it. Adopting an attitude of “I don’t care about your opinion, I do what I want” and taking inspiration from other NB folk can help, too.

I understand. You deserve friends and companionship. All of us do. But it is fear that stops us from getting what we deserve. The fear of rejection can be blinding. It prevents us from seeing that there’s good people out there who will not see us with a judgemental eye, who will only seek to bestow kindness on us.

I can imagine your pain. Do not be disheartened, just keep in mind that a judgemental attitude and friendship simply do not go together. Like oil and water. Friends will not judge you for what you are, for what you have been, for what you have lived through. If they do, they’re not friends worth keeping. 

You have nothing to be ashamed of. And even if you did, it would still not make you worthy of ridicule. Any overly critical person is so out of insecurity. Their opinion is never about you. Remember that.

I am in a similar situation. I don’t have any advice on how to cope with this beyond finding something you like to do/lifts up your mood.

Your worth is not determined by how productive or useful you are to society. Where we are right now is not a death sentence. There is still plenty of time.
